question.text: How many jobs will the U.S. economy add in November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the month-over-month change in number of employees on nonfarm payrolls, seasonally adjusted, reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics at its[ Employment Situation Summary](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm) for November 2026, rounded to the nearest thousand.
question.fine_print:
The question resolves based on initially-reported numbers and will not re-resolve if there are later revisions.

Typically, the number is reported in the first sentence of the BLS's press release. The numbers can also be found at [Table B-1. Employees on nonfarm payrolls by industry sector and selected industry detail](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.t17.htm) for *Total nonfarm* employees, *Seasonally adjusted.* For example, the number reported in the June 2026 release was 158,984,000 for June 2026 and 158,927,000 for May 2026. Hence the increase for that month was 57,000.

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46461) which opened on 2026-11-07 13:00:00.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-06: The BLS Employment Situation for October 2026 shows nonfarm payrolls up 165,000 and unemployment at 4.1%. August was revised from +133k to +186k and September from +29k to +60k, so the two months together were revised up 84k. The November 2026 report comes out **Friday, 2026-12-04 at 8:30 a.m. ET**. [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm)
- FRED PAYEMS has total nonfarm payrolls, seasonally adjusted, at 159,293k for October 2026 and 159,128k for September. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/PAYEMS.txt)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The November survey reference week is the pay period that includes November 12, so the data are still being collected.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-12: Initial jobless claims for the week ending Nov 7 rose 9k to 200k, against a 194-195k consensus. The 4-week average was unchanged at 195,250. Claims have been at or below 200k for nine weeks in a row. [AA](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/economy/us-weekly-jobless-claims-rise-to-200-000-above-expectations/4122947), [Tribstar](https://www.tribstar.com/region/u-s-jobless-claims-tick-up-to-200-000-but-remain-low-by-historic-standards/article_eea4adbd-f46c-5543-9527-1e3f14e30f5d.html)
- 2026-11-12: Challenger says 121,401 job cuts in 2026 through October were attributed to AI, about 20% of announced cuts. [Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2026/11/12/ai-layoffs-2026-so-far-job-cuts-firms-jobs-regions/)
- 2026-11-10: ADP's weekly NER Pulse had a 4-week average of +19,750 private jobs per week for the week ending Oct 24, and hiring strengthened for a second week. The next Pulse is due Nov 17 and should be the first with November weeks. [Finviz](https://finviz.com/news/420051/adp-national-employment-report-preliminary-estimate-for-october-24-2026)
- 2026-11-06: October's 165k far beat the LSEG consensus of 65k (the Reuters range was 35k to 125k).
  - Private payrolls rose 159k. Professional and business services added 70k, health care 41.6k, transportation and warehousing 24.8k, manufacturing 19k and government 6k.
  - Involuntary part-time work jumped 339k.
  - CME FedWatch put the odds of a December 8-9 Fed hike at about 77%.
  - The article mentions no strikes or one-off effects.
  [Fox Business](https://foxbusiness.com/economy/us-jobs-report-october-2026)
- Early November 2026 (Challenger October report): announced October cuts were 43,994, the lowest October since 2023 and down 71% from a year earlier. Seasonal hiring plans through October were 470,400, up 26%. Amazon plans more than 300k holiday hires, up 20%. [TradingEconomics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/challenger-job-cuts/news/598602), [SIA](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/amazon-to-hire-more-than-300000-in-holiday-season-up-20-from-last-year)
- 2026-11-04: ADP's monthly report showed private jobs up 86k in October, the same as September after September was revised. [SIA](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/private-sector-jobs-up-by-86000-workers-see-big-earnings-boost)
- I found no reports of a major strike, shutdown or weather disruption affecting November 2026.

## 4. Base rates
- **Current vintage of 2026 monthly changes** (worked out from FRED levels): Jan +160k, Feb -156k, Mar +214k, Apr +148k, May +63k, Jun +31k, Jul -10k, Aug +186k, Sep +60k, Oct +165k. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/PAYEMS.txt)
  - Year-to-date average is about 86k per month. The last 3 months average about 137k and the last 6 about 81k.
  - Month-to-month swings are large, with a standard deviation of roughly 110k in 2026.
- **Reuters, before the October report:** gains had averaged 68k a month in 2026, and breakeven job growth is estimated at about 40k or more per month.
- **Initial November prints in recent years** (from memory, not re-verified): 2021 +210k, 2022 +263k, 2023 +199k (lifted by returning auto strikers), 2024 +227k (lifted by the Boeing strike ending and hurricane rebound), 2025 +64k (distorted by the government shutdown).
- **Current-vintage October-to-November changes** (FRED): 2021 +658k, 2022 +303k, 2023 +127k, 2024 +134k, 2025 +41k. The data are seasonally adjusted, so there is no built-in November jump. However, recent Novembers have often been boosted by one-offs, and none is visible this year.
- **Surprise risk:** the October beat was about 100k over consensus. A gap of 50-100k between consensus and the first print is common.
- **Statistical baseline supplied with the question:** a median change of about +0.10%, which is roughly +160k on 159.3M, with p25 about +60k and p75 about +270k. This distribution includes the higher-growth years since 2005, so it probably sits above the current trend.

## 5. Other forecasts
- **Kalshi "Jobs numbers" for November 2026** (as of 2026-11-14): Above 20k 85%, 40k 79%, 50k 71%, 70k 62%, 80k 55%, 90k 48%, 100k 42%, 125k 30%. The implied median is about 85-90k.
- **Kalshi, revisions in the November report:** above 0 at 34%, above -50k at 69%.
- **Kalshi, November unemployment:** above 4.1% at 43%, above 4.2% at 10%.
- **Polymarket buckets:** <25k 18%, 25-50k 12.5%, 50-75k 13.5%, 75-100k 15%, 100-125k 15.5%, 125-150k 11.5%. That leaves about 14% for 150k or more, which is not listed.
- **Manifold:** 33% that payrolls rise by at least 150k. This looks high next to Kalshi (30% for above 125k) and Polymarket's implied ~14%.
- **Consensus:** I could not find a Reuters, Bloomberg or FactSet consensus for November 2026 yet. These usually appear in the week before the release.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **2026-11-17:** ADP NER Pulse, the first weekly data covering November.
- **2026-11-19:** jobless claims for the week ending Nov 14, which is the payroll survey reference week.
- **2026-11-25 and 2026-11-26** (likely, timing may shift around Thanksgiving): continuing claims and more weekly ADP data.
- **About 2026-12-02 to 2026-12-03:** ADP's monthly November report, the JOLTS release for October, Challenger's November report, and the ISM employment indexes.
- **2026-12-04 8:30 ET:** the BLS November report itself, which also revises September and October.
- The FOMC meeting on Dec 8-9 comes after resolution, but hike expectations shape how economists frame their previews.

I found no weather-related outlook that applies here.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 20 days remain. The BLS releases the November 2026 report on Friday, December 4, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET.

(b) The latest value is October 2026: +165k, initially reported November 6, 2026. The payroll level is 159,293k. August was revised to +186k and September to +60k.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be about +165k, a repeat of October. A flat payroll level would mean 0, but a repeat of October is the more relevant "no change" reading.

(d) If the trend continued:
- The last 3 months average about 137k.
- The year-to-date average is about 86k, and the last 6 months about 81k.
- A trend-weighted estimate is roughly 90-130k.

(e) Historical variation:
- In 2026, monthly changes had a standard deviation of about 110k, with values ranging from -156k to +214k.
- Gaps of 50-100k between the consensus and the first print are common.

(f) Expert and market expectations:
- Kalshi implies a median of about 85-90k: P(>20k) is 85%, P(>50k) 71%, P(>100k) 42% and P(>125k) 30%.
- Polymarket buckets imply a similar median of about 85k, with about 14% above 150k.
- Manifold puts 33% on at least 150k, which looks high next to the other markets.
- Labor indicators are firm: jobless claims are near 200k, Challenger cuts are low and seasonal hiring plans are strong.
- No formal economist consensus is available yet.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: October's beat turns out to be noise, with possible payback in professional and business services. AI-related cuts and a weaker seasonal adjustment around holiday hiring could produce a print near zero or negative, similar to February's -156k.
- High: Strong holiday hiring in retail and transportation, with Amazon planning 300k+ seasonal hires, combines with continued strength in health care and professional services to give a 200k+ print.

I anchor on the market median of about 88k and lean slightly upward because of the strong recent 3-month trend and low claims. I keep wide tails.
